title: The Keser as pleasure and desire: two sides of connecting yourself to something
overview:
Chapter 23 explains the *Keser* in detail: how it is the intermediary between the *ma'atzil* and the *ne'etzalim*. Its inner side, the three heads of *Atik Yomin*, is the end of the Infinite and stays above; its outer side, *Arich Anpin*, is the head of the emanations. They are one level and yet two, and the *mashal* is pleasure and desire.

Every desire has a pleasure behind it, so pleasure seems to be the inner thing; but what a person does not want he does not enjoy, like the kid banging pots and pans, whose noise only he enjoys. Neither exists without the other, so they are one entity: both are you connecting yourself to something. The soul is drawn after pleasure and flees pain so completely that the early Kabbalists called pleasure its essence. It is not quite: pleasure fills the essence and draws it out, and it is what keeps every power alive, kindness, cruelty, winning and intellect alike. Only the will is needed for the pleasure in turn, and it is not known which comes first.

sections.title: The Keser in detail: the end of the ma'atzil within, the head of the ne'etzalim without
sections.summary: Chapter 23 begins to explain the *Keser* (crown) in detail: how it is the intermediary between the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates) and the *ne'etzalim* (the emanations). Its inner side, the three heads of *Atik Yomin*, is the last level of the *ma'atzil* and stays above; its outer side is the root and head of the *ne'etzalim*.

blocks.text:
Chapter 23 begins to explain *Keser* (crown), *ratzon* (will, desire) and *taanug* (delight, pleasure): how *Keser* is the intermediary between the *ma'atzil* (the one who emanates), the source of the light, and the *ne'etzalim* (the emanations), the lights of *Atzilus*.

*Keser* was mentioned before in general; **now in detail**. It contains **the end of the ma'atzil**, the lowest level of the emanator, and that is **the inner aspect of the Keser**.

**On the other hand, the Keser is also the root and the head, the beginning of the ne'etzalim**, the first of the *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) to leave the *ma'atzil*: **that's the external part of the Keser**. With these two aspects it is the intermediary, as *Etz Chaim* (the Arizal's Tree of Life) explains.

phrases.en: and it's also known, it's common knowledge

are separate and they're removed and they remain above,
and they are not enclothed in the *ne'etzalim*, they do not descend into the *ne'etzalim*.
and this is what it means, this is what it says in the *posuk*, that G-d transcends, He is above, raised above the days of the world.
and that's why it is called *Atik Yomin*,
the one that uproots mountains,
that he's removed from the days of the world.
So all this is known, it's common knowledge

blocks.text:
As *Etz Chaim* says, the *gimmel rishin* (three heads) of *Atik Yomin*, the *Keser*, *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) of *Atik*, which are the *pnimiyus* (inner side) of *Keser*, **are separate** and **remain above**: **they do not descend into the ne'etzalim.**

That is why G-d is called raised above **the days of the world**, the *middos* (emotional attributes) of *Atzilus*. The *middos* of *Atik* already relate to the world; its three heads are above that.

**That's why it is called Atik Yomin.** It is usually translated "the Ancient of Days", but *atik* can mean old, removed, or to copy. Here it means removed from the days of the world, the *middos*, as in **the one that uproots mountains**.

**So all this is known**: the *pnimiyus* of *Keser*, removed from the world, is the end of the *ma'atzil*; its *chitzoniyus* (outer side), which relates to the world, is the root and head of the *ne'etzalim*.

As usual, the Mitteler Rebbe opens a topic with its sources and basic kabbalistic terms, and only then gives the *meshalim* (analogies) and explanations. Having quoted *Etz Chaim*, he now adds what is almost a question.

sections.title: One level or two? Atik Yomin is the pleasure, Arich Anpin the desire
sections.summary: *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are counted as one level, the *Keser*, and yet *Atik* is the end of the Infinite and *Arich* the head of the emanations. The explanation is the *mashal* of *taanug* (pleasure), which stands for *Atik*, and *ratzon* (desire), which stands for *Arich*.

phrases.en: because on the one hand we see that *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are considered one level,

phrases.he: רק שבכללות נחשב בחינת עתיק יומין מסוף עולם האין סוף,
phrases.en: but in general we consider *Atik Yomin* to be the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, the end of the world of the infinite,

phrases.he: ובחינת אריך אנפין הוא שרש וראש לנאצלים,

blocks.text: **We have to understand this in a detailed way.** *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are **considered one level**: *Keser* is one level. **But in general we consider Atik Yomin to be the end of the world of the Ein Sof**, the infinite, **and we consider Arich Anpin to be the root and the head, the beginning, for the ne'etzalim, for the limited worlds**, as *Etz Chaim* says.

blocks.question: So is the Keser one level, or is it two levels?
blocks.text: Obviously it is both. *Keser* is one level: *Atik* and *Arich Anpin* are not two things. Yet the two aspects are distinct: as *Atik Yomin* it is removed, as *Arich Anpin* it is enclothed in the worlds. How that works is what we have to understand, and now he begins a *mashal* (analogy) to explain it.

phrases.en: and the explanation of these matters is known,
that the *mashal* for this is pleasure and desire.

blocks.title: Pleasure and desire
blocks.text: **The explanation of these matters is known**: **the mashal for this is pleasure and desire**, pleasure for *Atik Yomin* and desire for *Arich Anpin*.

sections.title: Which is inside? Every desire has a pleasure in it, and nothing is enjoyed without being wanted
sections.summary: Since nobody would want riches or honor if they gave no pleasure, the pleasure seems to be the inner cause of the desire. But a thing a person does not want he does not enjoy at all, so the desire seems to be the inner cause of the pleasure.

phrases.he: ולהיות שאנו רואים שבכל רצון יש תענוג,
phrases.en: and being that we see that every desire has a pleasure in it, has a pleasure behind it,

phrases.he: ולולי התענוג לא היה רצון לדבר כלל
phrases.en: and if it wasn't for that pleasure, then you wouldn't want it at all.
for example the desire for riches, or the desire for honor, for glory,
if it wouldn't be that there was a pleasure,
you wouldn't want it at all.

blocks.text: **Every desire has a pleasure in it, has a pleasure behind it, and if it wasn't for that pleasure, then you wouldn't want it at all.** You want a thing because you will enjoy it. **For example the desire for riches, or the desire for honor**: were it no fun to be rich or to be honored, **you wouldn't want it at all**.

blocks.title: The tax form and the autographs
blocks.text: If being rich were only a nuisance and a complicated tax form, people would not want it. If fame were only a pain, people taking your picture all the time and wanting your signature, nobody would want it.

phrases.he: אם כן התענוג הוא בחינת פנימיות הרצון
phrases.en: if so, that means that the pleasure is the inner thing of the *ratzon*.
seemingly.

blocks.text:
**If so, that means that the pleasure is the inner thing of the ratzon.** **Seemingly.** What gives rise to the desire is the pleasure you can get from the thing, so the pleasure is the inner cause, the *pnimiyus*, and the desire its outcome: first he enjoys riches or honor, then comes the desire for them, to get that pleasure.

So it seems. But it is not that simple.

phrases.en: but however, we also see the opposite,
We see that if a person does not have a desire for something, he will not enjoy it.

phrases.he: שהרי דבר שלא ירצה בו לא יתענג ממנו
phrases.en: if a person doesn't want something, he will not delight in it, he won't enjoy it,
at all.
If so, that means that the desire is the inner thing of the *taanug*,

blocks.text: **But however, we also see the opposite**: **if a person doesn't want something, he will not delight in it, he won't enjoy it, at all.** **If so, that means that the desire is the inner thing of the taanug**: whether you enjoy something depends on whether you wanted it.

blocks.title: Food stuffed down the throat
blocks.text: Even something normally pleasurable is not enjoyed if a person does not want it. In *halacha* (Jewish law), one who has food stuffed down his throat against his will has no *hanaa* (benefit, enjoyment), which matters where the only problem is getting *hanaa*. So whenever somebody is forced to do something.

blocks.title: The kid banging pots and pans
blocks.text: A kid banging on pots and pans makes noise, not music, yet he enjoys it and everybody else hates it: he wants to make the noise, and they do not want it.

blocks.title: The favorite CD
blocks.text:
Music is the opposite case, inherently pleasurable, yet someone who wants quiet right now finds even his favorite CD painful. You could say his mood makes it painful, so he does not want it because he does not enjoy it.

But take someone who becomes *frum* (religiously observant) and no longer wants non-Jewish music: when someone puts it on in the room, he is often disturbed by it. Nothing made him stop liking it; he just does not want it. So when you decide you want something, you enjoy it.

sections.title: Neither exists without the other, so they are one: two sides of connecting yourself to something
sections.summary: Since neither desire nor pleasure exists without the other, they must be one *mahus* (entity). Both are the self connecting to something: desire while it is not yet had, pleasure once it is, and the connection itself is a third, higher thing, the *Radla*. This holds for simple and essential pleasure and desire and for the *murkav* (composite) kind alike.

phrases.en: and on the other hand, we see
that you cannot have one without the other.

phrases.he: כי אין לרצון קיום בלא תענוג ואין לתענוג קיום בלא רצון
phrases.en: You can't have a desire without a pleasure, and you can't have a pleasure without a desire.
based on this,
We must say that they are really one entity.

phrases.he: מאחר שמאמצעות חיבורם יחד דוקא יתקיים כו'
phrases.en: because they can only exist when you have them both together.

blocks.text: So pleasure seemed the *pnimiyus*, and then *ratzon* did. Now he says **you cannot have one without the other**: **you can't have a desire without a pleasure, and you can't have a pleasure without a desire.** Neither is a *pnimiyus* standing alone with the other coming from it; they are always interdependent.

**Based on this**, **we must say that they are really one entity**, **because they can only exist when you have them both together.** Were desire and pleasure separate, you could have one without the other, and you never do; one may be dominant, but they are always together, two sides of the same coin.

*Ratzon* and *taanug* both mean connecting yourself to something outside yourself. If it is something you do not have yet, or that is not fully revealed, it is *ratzon*: you go towards it; when you get it, it is pleasure. You get the pleasure because you want it, and want it because of the pleasure, since both come from a third, higher thing: that you connect yourself to it.

blocks.title: It's his sound
blocks.text:
So the kid with the pots and pans enjoys it because he wants it: he decided to do it and put himself into it, so the sound is beautiful to him, "'cause it's his sound."

And where the desire is less clear and you mainly see the pleasure, a person enjoys something because he associates himself with it, because it reminds him somehow of himself; seeing himself in it, he goes after it.

This inner thing that connects the two, his association with the thing, is the third head mentioned later: besides *Atik* and *Arich* there is *Radla*, *Reisha d'lo isyada*, the head that is not known, the innermost *pnimiyus* of *Keser*, where you connect yourself to the thing.

blocks.title: The mouth and the stomach
blocks.text:
If you do not want something right now, it is because you would not enjoy it right now. The desire to eat is amplified by hunger, and when you are full, eating hurts and the *taanug* is gone. Yet eat quickly when very hungry, and your mouth still wants more while your stomach is full and it hurts.

That is a fight between two desires, the mouth's and the stomach's: it takes time for the stomach to tell the mouth to stop, and sweet things especially make you want more. But that is already a *ratzon murkav* (a composite will), many desires with a reason, not the *etzem ratzon* or the *etzem taanug*, with a whole lot of *sechel* (intellect) involved: the whole matter of *Tikun*, touched on already.

phrases.he: וכל זה בין בתענוג ורצון פשוט ועצמי,
phrases.en: And all of this applies whether you're speaking about an essential and simple pleasure and desire,
or whether you're speaking about a pleasure and desire that is *murkav*, it's complex,
that the soul is spread and drawn after it,
even though it's not something connected to yourself,

blocks.text:
**All of this applies whether you're speaking about an essential and simple pleasure and desire, or… a pleasure and desire that is murkav, it's complex**: based on a reason, this much of one and that much of another, a whole system of desires about something separate from you.

An essential *ratzon* and *taanug* is part of you: you desire part of yourself, like the *chafetz chesed* (the desire for kindness) of chapter 10. You want to be a nice person; you enjoy being nice.

The *ratzon murkav* goes out of you: **the soul is spread and drawn after it, even though it's not something connected to yourself**; **it's something separate**, like money or food, a good piece of chocolate cake or ice cream. Either way, *ratzon* and *taanug* are one thing.

sections.title: The soul is drawn after pleasure and flees pain: it looks as if pleasure is its essence
sections.summary: The soul's nature is to be drawn after anything pleasurable, until its whole self is caught up in it, even in a pleasure separate from it like honor, money or winning; and it runs from pain to exactly the same degree. So the soul seems to be a *hiyuli* (raw potential) for pleasure, and the early Kabbalists declared that pleasure is its essence and nothing is higher.

phrases.en: however,

phrases.he: בכלל אנו רואים שהנפש טבעה להתמשך אחר דבר שיש בו תענוג,
phrases.en: In general, we see that the nature of the soul is that it's drawn after anything that is pleasurable,

phrases.he: עד שיכול להיות כל עצמותה נמשך ונכלל בו
phrases.en: until a person's whole self, their whole essence can get caught up in this pleasure,
when it's a *taanug murkav* in just a very specific thing that's separate from themselves,
For example, let's say honor,
Or money,
Or it could be in other things, in *chachma*,
*Hispaarus* means to show off.
and so too with any other *midda*,

like the *taava* for any of the pleasures of this world.

blocks.text: **In general, we see that the nature of the soul is that it's drawn after anything that is pleasurable, until a person's whole self, their whole essence can get caught up in this pleasure.** Most powerfully, even **when it's a taanug murkav in just a very specific thing that's separate from themselves**, a person can become totally obsessed with it.

**For example, let's say honor**: for some people honor and fame become their whole life. **Or money**: a separate thing, yet the pleasure in it consumes them. **Or… in chachma**: the classic professor, whose whole life is his intellectual work. In *middos*, some live to be kind, *chesed*, some for *din* (judgement), justice; in *netzach* (victory) some are very competitive, always one up. **Hispaarus means to show off**: some need everybody to praise them and ooh and ahh. **And so too with any other midda**: *yesod*, a teacher whose whole life is giving over; *Malchus*, to be a king.
Or it is **something that the soul covets**, **like the taava** (craving) **for any of the pleasures of this world**: food, any physical thing, in which a person can get totally caught up.

phrases.he: אף על פי שכל אלה אינן בבחינת עצמיות התענוג ההיולי,
phrases.en: even though none of these things are essential pleasures coming from the *taanug hiyuli*, from the essential *taanug*,
just that the soul is drawn after these things and it craves them, or it covets them.

phrases.he: אבל מזה נראה שעצם הנפש הוא בבחינת תענוג ההיולי
phrases.en: But from this, that the soul is drawn after anything pleasurable, we see that the soul is like a *hiyuli* for pleasure, it's like the essence of pleasure.

phrases.he: על כן תומשך אחר עונג מורכב
phrases.en: and therefore the soul will be drawn after any pleasure, even a *oneg murkav*, even something separate from it,
and it will run away from pain,
which is the opposite of pleasure.

blocks.text: **None of these things are essential pleasures coming from the taanug hiyuli, from the essential taanug**; it is **just that the soul is drawn after these things and it craves them**. **But from this, that the soul is drawn after anything pleasurable, we see that the soul is like a hiyuli for pleasure, it's like the essence of pleasure.**

**Therefore the soul will be drawn after any pleasure, even a oneg murkav, even something separate from it, and it will run away from pain, which is the opposite of pleasure.** The soul is this ability for pleasure: not quite its essence, as will be said, but almost. It goes after anything pleasurable because that is what it is, and flees pain, which takes the soul out of the thing.

phrases.he: עד שב' קוין שקולין הן ממש
phrases.en: to the point that these are two equally weighed lines, that these two polar opposites of pleasure and pain are totally equal.

phrases.he: שכפי ערך התפשטות הנפש במלאת אורה בדברי תענוג,
phrases.en: that to the exact same extent that the soul, its light, becomes full from something that's pleasurable,

phrases.he: כן תתכווץ ותתמעט אורה בצער ויגון בתכלית כו'
phrases.en: So too with the reverse, that something that's painful can cause a person to totally remove themselves, and it diminishes the light of the soul,

blocks.text: **These are two equally weighed lines**: pleasure and pain, polar opposites, are totally equal. **To the exact same extent that the soul, its light, becomes full from something that's pleasurable**, putting itself into all its *sechel* and *middos*, a great *hispashtus* (spreading forth), **so too with the reverse**: pain **diminishes the light of the soul**. A person in pain withdraws into himself, uses neither *sechel* nor *middos*, and everything becomes dry and mechanical.

That is why something traumatic can make a person withdraw, perhaps from life in general, until his soul no longer expresses itself; while a big pleasure brings out all his qualities, and he does everything better, with much more life and energy.
This is what *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) does in G-dliness: it reveals the G-dly *taanug* in everything, and so brings much more vitality into everything.

phrases.en: from this we see,
this shows us the essential nature of the soul
that it is pleasure.
and the main proof,
is the fact that the soul will run away and be withdrawn from pain.
this is more of a proof than the pleasure,

blocks.text: **From this we see**, **this shows us the essential nature of the soul**, **that it is pleasure**. **And the main proof is the fact that the soul will run away and be withdrawn from pain.** **This is more of a proof than the pleasure**: from the pull of pleasure you could say the soul is something else and pleasure only a bonus; that pain takes the soul away shows that this is what it is.

phrases.he: ועל כן גזרו אומר המקובלים הראשונים, שהתענוג נחשב מעצם הנפש,
phrases.en: And therefore, the early Kabbalists declared that pleasure is the essence of the soul.
and they said,

blocks.text: **And therefore, the early Kabbalists declared that pleasure is the essence of the soul**, **and they said, there's nothing higher than pleasure.**

sections.title: But it is not so: pleasure fills the essence and draws it out, until the soul can expire
sections.summary: The Mitteler Rebbe answers that pleasure is not really the essence of the soul. The essence is higher; great pleasure fills it and draws it out, until it is almost wholly spent in the thing, as in *klos hanefesh* (the soul's expiring), and intense pain can spend it completely too.

phrases.en: and this is not true, it's not true that it's really the essence of the soul, and it's not true that it's the highest level.

phrases.he: רק שהעצמיות דנפש תתמלא מן התענוג הרב
phrases.en: Rather, the essence of the soul is really higher, but the essence of the soul is filled from great pleasure.
and it's drawn after something that's pleasurable, and it puts its whole essence into it, its whole self into it,
to the point that it will almost completely lose itself in the thing,
like it says *kalsa nafshi*,

blocks.text: **And this is not true**: **it's not true that it's really the essence of the soul, and it's not true that it's the highest level.** It is the deepest level of the soul that is expressed. The Mitteler Rebbe is not saying they were wrong, only that the statement is relative, not literally true.

**Rather, the essence of the soul is really higher, but the essence of the soul is filled from great pleasure**: the more pleasure, the more the essence comes out, **and it puts its whole essence into it… to the point that it will almost completely lose itself in the thing, like it says kalsa nafshi** (my soul expired). That is *klos hanefesh*: from a great G-dly pleasure the soul is so drawn after it that it leaves the body, and the person dies.

blocks.title: Klos hanefesh comes from the revelations, not the essence
blocks.text: This happens only from the *giluyim* (revelations) of G-dliness, which are more in the higher worlds, so a great pleasure in them draws the soul up and away from the body. The essence of G-dliness is found *davka* (precisely) in the physical world, since G-d chose a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). Recognizing that brings *shov* (return) rather than *ratzo* (running out): the soul wants to be here, and its pleasure here is greater, for here there is *hasagas hamahus* (a grasp of the essence) of G-d Himself. One who does not appreciate that can have *klos hanefesh*.

phrases.en: and on the other hand,
the soul can also be completely exhausted, completely burnt up, with the diminishing of the light completely,
through and through,
from intense pain,

blocks.text: **And on the other hand, the soul can also be completely exhausted… with the diminishing of the light completely, through and through, from intense pain.** That too is *klos hanefesh*. In depression a person loses his pleasure in life and his soul is removed from his body, so far that he can actually die.

blocks.title: Spouses who die one after the other
blocks.text: Sometimes a husband and wife are so connected that when one dies, G-d forbid, the other dies shortly after. The pleasure in the person was so great, and losing him so painful, that the soul is drawn out of the body: the whole self was connected to this pleasure, and the pain takes it away.

blocks.title: The dog on the boy's grave
blocks.text: Even with animals. A boy and his dog were very close. The boy was killed in a car accident; a little later the dog disappeared, and they found him lying on the boy's grave, the last place he saw him. The dog's whole pleasure was his boy, and losing him took his whole life away.
And the other side too: someone with a great pleasure in something will forget and drop everything else and put himself totally into it.

sections.title: A clearer proof: the pleasure in each power is what keeps it alive
sections.summary: In every particular power of the soul, the pleasure in it is what keeps it existing: the kind man lives from his pleasure in doing good, the cruel man from his pleasure in cruelty, the competitor from winning, until if he loses he gets sick. So too intellect: without the pleasure in it a person cannot come up with any *chachma*, and the moisture over the brain, the *hiyuli* of pleasure, is the source of all intellect and makes the wise man's face shine.

phrases.he: וראיה ברורה יותר ממה שאנו רואים שגם בפרטי כחות של הנפש, הנה בחינת העונג שבזה הכח בפרטות, הוא עיקר קיום מציאותו תמיד
phrases.en: And even a clearer proof for this is that we see that even with each of the individual powers of the soul, the pleasure in this power is the main thing that keeps it going, that gives it its strength.
for example, the attribute of kindness,

phrases.he: גם שהוא עצמי וטבעי בטבע הטוב להטיב,
phrases.en: even though we say that it's an essential part of a person's nature that he's a nice person,
the main thing that maintains this *midda*, this nature, is the pleasure
that he derives a great pleasure from giving, bestowing goodness.
and this is really what maintains this nature.

phrases.he: שהוא מה שטבעו להתענג ביותר מן ההטבה,
phrases.en: that his nature is to derive a lot of pleasure from bestowing goodness,

phrases.he: עד שכל עיקר חיותו בנפשו בא על ידי עונג זה
phrases.en: to the point that the main vitality of his soul, his whole life, comes through this pleasure
of goodness and kindness.

blocks.text: **And even a clearer proof**: **even with each of the individual powers of the soul, the pleasure in this power is the main thing that keeps it going.** **For example, the attribute of kindness**: **even though we say that it's an essential part of a person's nature that he's a nice person**, **the main thing that maintains this midda… is the pleasure**, **that he derives a great pleasure from giving, bestowing goodness.**

**This is really what maintains this nature**: being a nice person means he gets so much pleasure from doing nice things that he wants to do them all the time, **to the point that the main vitality of his soul, his whole life, comes through this pleasure of goodness and kindness.**

This does not mean he wants only the pleasure and not the kindness: his pleasure is in the other person being helped, not in helping himself. It means he associates himself with kindness. That is who he is, and his whole sense of self, his whole ego in no negative sense, comes through kindness.

So the more kindness he does, the more pleasure, because each kindness expresses the self he sees: a nice person. And again, his sense of self is that he is selfless, so this takes nothing from the selflessness of his kindness. This is not someone who does kindness so that people will praise him; he really wants the kindness.

phrases.en: and on the other side,
somebody that's naturally cruel,

phrases.he: אין זה רק שזהו כל חיותו בתענוג זה שעושה רע ואכזריות, כידוע

blocks.text: **And on the other side, somebody that's naturally cruel**: inflicting pain makes him feel great, makes him feel big, and the more cruelty he can impose on people, or animals, the happier he is.

phrases.en: the same thing with the attribute of competitiveness, conquering, that he wants to win.

phrases.he: כל עיקר קיומו רק העונג המופלג,
phrases.en: What makes a person want to be competitive and to win is that he gets a great pleasure from winning.

phrases.he: עד שחיות נפשו נמשך כולה בזה
phrases.en: until his whole vitality of his soul is drawn into this.
that he beats the other person.
and if he will not win,
then he'll get sick,

blocks.text: **The same thing with the attribute of competitiveness, conquering, that he wants to win.** **What makes a person want to be competitive and to win is that he gets a great pleasure from winning.** Someone who does not see himself as a winner will not get such pleasure. But for one who is very into winning, it is his whole self, what makes him significant, so winning is a great pleasure and failing very painful, **until his whole vitality of his soul is drawn into this**, **that he beats the other person**.
**And if he will not win, then he'll get sick**: losing disturbs him so much that it makes him ill.

Rabbi Walters thinks you see this with a lot of world champions. Some are good sports who enjoy the game. But some, apparently like Bobby Fischer with chess, made winning their whole self, their whole ego: to crush the other person, viciously, and even get sick over losing.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בכל פרטי פרטי המדות
phrases.en: and so it is with all of the little minute details of the *middos*, all the individual *middos*,
even including *chachma* and *ratzon*, even intellect and desire.
the main thing that keeps them, that maintains them, the main maintaining force and their main source is the pleasure that a person gets in this.
and if it wouldn't be for the pleasure a person derived from intellect, from getting an understanding of something, or arriving at a new idea,

phrases.he: אין לו כח לחדש שום חכמה,
phrases.en: he would not be able to originate any sort of *chachma*,
like we see tangibly,

blocks.text: **And so it is with all of the little minute details of the middos… even including chachma and ratzon**: **the main maintaining force and their main source is the pleasure that a person gets in this.** **If it wouldn't be for the pleasure a person derived from intellect**, from understanding or a new idea, **he would not be able to originate any sort of chachma, like we see tangibly.**

phrases.en: like it says in the *Gemara*,
if it wouldn't be for the joy of study, then I would not be able to learn so well.

blocks.text: **Like it says in the Gemara**, in the words of one of the sages of the *Talmud*: **if it wouldn't be for the joy of study, then I would not be able to learn so well.**

It is not a matter of discipline. You can force yourself to do something, but to be good at it and accomplish you have to be invested in it. Forcing yourself does help, because it comes from your *koach haratzon* (power of will), which is the same thing as *taanug*: you connect yourself to it, and the effort gives you pleasure in it. But that is not the point here.

The point here is straight: without the pleasure, he will not be good at it. A person who does not enjoy a subject has his mind off; he hears the words without thinking, so he will not understand or come up with ideas. One who enjoys it puts his whole mind into it, gets an intimate feel for the idea, understands it properly and comes up with ideas.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין חכמת אדם תאיר פניו,
phrases.en: and as is known, the idea that it says that the wisdom of a person enlightens his face,
because the liquid, the liquid that's over the brain,
this liquid is physically the *hiyuli* of *taanug*, it's the essence of pleasure.

phrases.he: הוא המקור להשכיל כל שכל כו'
phrases.en: And that liquid is also the source of *sechel*, of intellect,

blocks.text: **As is known, the idea that it says that the wisdom of a person enlightens his face**: an idea makes the face shine, and the face of a *chacham b'etzem* (wise in essence) is always shining. **Because the liquid** between skull and brain **is physically the hiyuli of taanug, it's the essence of pleasure. And that liquid is also the source of sechel**, the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight).

Membranes over the brain filter this liquid, and how it is filtered activates *sechel* (more on this later). When it reaches the brain it both triggers thought and gives pleasure. So intellect is a localized, specific pleasure, a pleasure in a certain form, and that pleasure comes out as a shining face, with more blood flow to it.

A very happy or excited person's face shines, as a drink turns the face red, and different pleasures give different colors. So a very wise person has a certain glow from this pleasure, and so does a very kind one: he is always happy, because he enjoys life, even the painful parts.

sections.title: Only the will is needed for the pleasure: the two are one essence, and it is not known which comes first
sections.summary: Pleasure keeps every power going, but only the will is also needed for pleasure: without wanting it, a person does not enjoy kindness, study, winning, money or honor. Both are the whole soul drawn after a thing, so whatever opposes the will is painful and whatever is enjoyed is wanted; they are one *mahus*, sometimes one inner and sometimes the other, never one without the other, whether simple or *murkav*.

phrases.en: however,

phrases.he: ברצון בלבד אנו רואים שבלא רצון אין תענוג
phrases.en: unique is *ratzon* among all of the *kochos* of the *nefesh*, that only with *ratzon* do we see that without *ratzon* there will be no *taanug*.
and this we see even with all the *pratei middos*,

blocks.text: **However**, **unique is ratzon among all of the kochos of the nefesh** (the powers of the soul), **that only with ratzon do we see that without ratzon there will be no taanug.** *Taanug* keeps all the powers going, but only *ratzon* is also a source of *taanug*: without *chachma* you still have *taanug*; without *ratzon* you do not.

If you do not enjoy *chachma* or *bina* you will not have them: you will not understand, or be good at logic. But without *bina* or *chachma* you still have *taanug*. It is one-way: *taanug* keeps the *sechel* and *middos* going, but you do not need them to have *taanug*. You don't have to be smart to enjoy things, and being smarter does not mean more *taanug*. With *ratzon*, though, if you do not want something you will not enjoy it. **And this we see even with all the pratei middos** (the particular attributes).

phrases.he: כמו אם לא ירצה בחסד או דין אין לו בו תענוג כלל
phrases.en: if you don't want *chesed* or if you don't want *din*, you won't enjoy it.
and also if he doesn't want to study, he doesn't want to come up with ideas now,
you won't enjoy it at all.

phrases.he: וכן אם לא ירצה בניצוח כלל
phrases.en: And if a person doesn't want to win at all,
then he won't have a pleasure in winning.
And the same thing with showing off.
and the same thing with the other pleasures of this world,
like money and honor and the like,

phrases.he: בלא רצון אין תענוג בהן כלל וכלל
phrases.en: if a person doesn't want them, then he won't enjoy them at all.

blocks.text: **If you don't want chesed or if you don't want din, you won't enjoy it.** Even someone who normally enjoys *chesed* will not enjoy it when he does not want it, say because it will be bad for him. **And also if he doesn't want to study, he doesn't want to come up with ideas now, you won't enjoy it at all.**

blocks.title: Playing with a little kid
blocks.text: **If a person doesn't want to win at all, then he won't have a pleasure in winning**: playing with a little kid, you want him to win, so winning yourself gives you no pleasure. **And the same thing with showing off**: if you want people to make a big deal about you, you enjoy it; if you want to keep things quiet, it makes you uncomfortable.

**And the same thing with the other pleasures of this world, like money and honor and the like**: **if a person doesn't want them, then he won't enjoy them at all.** Money is then only a headache, and so too honor.

phrases.he: והיינו מפני שכללות ענין זה הוא בהיות שכל עיקר עצם הנפש נמשך אחר התענוג והרצון,
phrases.en: And this is because the general idea is that with all the *middos* it's really one thing, that the *etzem hanefesh* goes after *taanug* and *ratzon*.

phrases.he: (שהרצון הוא גם כן המשכת כל הנפש
phrases.en: that *ratzon* is also the idea of drawing your whole soul into something.

phrases.he: עד שכולה תכלה ברצון לדבר מה כו׳ כידוע)
phrases.en: To the point where a person can be totally obsessed with the *ratzon* for something.

phrases.he: על כן גם בכל פרטי כחותיה,
phrases.en: and therefore also with every one of the soul's powers,
their main existence or continuance comes from the pleasure and the desire.

blocks.text: **And this is because the general idea is that with all the middos it's really one thing, that the etzem hanefesh** (the essence of the soul) **goes after taanug and ratzon.** Where you have them you put yourself into a thing; without them it gives no pleasure. For **ratzon is also the idea of drawing your whole soul into something**, **to the point where a person can be totally obsessed with the ratzon for something**.

*Taanug* and *ratzon* mean connecting and investing yourself in something: the more of them, the more you succeed and express yourself there, the soul's light spreading into it. That is why they are said to be like the *etzem hanefesh*: not the essence itself, but what connects it to something else. Two sides of one coin: *ratzon* goes out to the thing; *taanug* is what comes back to you from it.

In *ratzon* your connection to the thing is felt as a void, and you rush to fill the form you chose. Once you have it and have filled that form, you get the pleasure of feeling yourself in it, that it expresses you. **And therefore also with every one of the soul's powers, their main existence or continuance comes from the pleasure and the desire.**

phrases.en: And when the *taanug* and *ratzon* are missing in something, then this thing is painful.
the opposite of pleasure.
something that opposes a person's desire,
even if it's not essentially painful,
he'll automatically be very pained.

blocks.text: **When the taanug and ratzon are missing in something, then this thing is painful**, **the opposite of pleasure.** And **something that opposes a person's desire, even if it's not essentially painful, he'll automatically be very pained.**

blocks.title: The friend who stops you in a rush
blocks.text: You are in a rush to do something you are excited about, not even a meeting you might miss, and a friend stops you to talk for a minute. Talking to him is no pain; you enjoy it. But right now he keeps you from what you want, so it is very painful and you are eaten up: painful automatically, because it stops what you want.

phrases.he: כמו אם ירצה לאהוב שונאו, יתענג ממנו
phrases.en: For example, if a person wants to love his enemy, he'll take pleasure in him.
or if somebody doesn't want his beloved,
then he'll get pain from him.

phrases.he: וכן אם יתענג בשנאוי לו המזיקו, ירצה בו,
phrases.en: Similarly, we see with pleasure that if a person enjoys something, even if it's something that's hateful to him, that hurts him, he'll want it.

phrases.he: ואם יצטער באהוב לו, לא ירצה
phrases.en: and if a person gets pain from something that's beloved to him, something that he likes, he won't want it.

blocks.text: **For example, if a person wants to love his enemy, he'll take pleasure in him.** **Or if somebody doesn't want his beloved**, **then he'll get pain from him**. Want your enemy for something and you enjoy his company; and the company of someone you like, like the friend who stops you in a rush, is painful when you do not want it.

Likewise, **if a person enjoys something, even if it's something that's hateful to him, that hurts him, he'll want it.** People develop a pleasure in alcohol or drugs: at first it tastes bad, it is disgusting and it totally messes you up, but because some pleasure comes from it, you want it.

blocks.title: Donating blood
blocks.text: **And if a person gets pain from something that's beloved to him, something that he likes, he won't want it.** A very kind person donates blood, and it hurts, or makes him faint a little; because of that pain he no longer wants to, and is kind of afraid to.

phrases.he: כי מהות אחד הן הרצון והתענוג,
phrases.en: because the *ratzon* and *taanug* are really one thing.
It's not that we don't know, it's not known. In other words, it's impossible to know which one came first.
And sometimes one is internal, the other one is external.
and sometimes you see the other way around.
but you'll never find one without the other.
If there's no pleasure, there's no desire,
and if there's no desire, there's no pleasure.
Whether it's a simple desire and pleasure, or whether it's a *murkav*, a complex desire and pleasure, meaning something separate from yourself,
like we said before,
And that is enough for the understanding.

blocks.text: **Because the ratzon and taanug are really one thing**: connecting yourself to something. **It's not that we don't know, it's not known… it's impossible to know which one came first.** **And sometimes one is internal, the other one is external**, one manifest and the other the hidden cause, **and sometimes you see the other way around**: now *ratzon* looks like the *chitzoniyus* and *taanug* the *pnimiyus*, now the reverse.

**But you'll never find one without the other. If there's no pleasure, there's no desire, and if there's no desire, there's no pleasure**, **whether it's a simple desire and pleasure, or whether it's a murkav**, about something separate from yourself. Both express your connecting yourself with something. **And that is enough for the understanding.** The *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) comes in the next chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: How is the *Keser* an intermediary, and which of its two sides is the end of the *ma'atzil* and which the head of the *ne'etzalim*?
What can the word *atik* mean, and in what sense are the three heads of *Atik Yomin* removed from "the days of the world"?
What do the food stuffed down someone's throat, the kid banging pots and pans and the favorite CD show about desire and pleasure?
Why must desire and pleasure be one entity, and what is the third, higher thing they both come from?
Why is the soul's running away from pain more of a proof than its being drawn after pleasure?
What is unique about *ratzon* among the powers of the soul, compared with *chachma* and *bina*?

notes.text: The second class opens in the middle of a point ("Yeah, I mean right now if you don't want it, because you wouldn't enjoy it so much right now", 02 w0-18), as if answering a question that is not on the tape. It continues the first class's discussion of desire and pleasure and is placed, with outOfPlace, under lines 13-14 as the mashal of the mouth and the stomach.

A few remarks in the fourth class sound like answers to a listener who is not heard: "Well, it's not a matter of being disciplined" (04 w169), "Like when you drink, your face gets red. Yeah, that's what I mean" (04 w708-720), "No, you don't have to be smart to enjoy things. Right?" (04 w1021-1031). They are written as his own points, not as student questions.
At 01 w881-892 the transcript has "Now the Maggid will begin giving a mashal"; it is presumably a slip, or the machine's hearing, for the Mitteler Rebbe. The block says "he".

Phrases read without English: line 17's "ומדות בחסד ודין וניצוח" (he explains each with examples instead), line 18's closing "וכהאי גוונא", line 28's "כידוע" and line 32's "אין זה רק ... כידוע" (he explains it as "what does it mean..."). Line 33's second phrase cites his explanation right after the reading (03 w1620-1639), "what makes a person want to be competitive and to win is that he gets a great pleasure from winning", his only rendering of it. Line 50's second phrase cites his correction of himself ("It's not that we don't know, it's not known"). Line 1's second phrase cites "now to explain the details of Keser" (01 w87-94), his rendering of בפרטיות בחינת הכתר after a word about the Keser having been mentioned in general before; the leading "but" is dropped.

01 w1710-1731: the transcript has "even if they just decide they want to listen to it, they also won't enjoy it"; from what follows (the newly frum man who does not want to hear the music) he means "decide they don't want to", and the block says so.

Sources as he gives them: "it says in the posuk" for "raised above the days of the world" (line 4); "like it says in the Gemara... one of the sages of the Talmud said it" for "ilmalei chedvasa dishmatsa" (line 37); "the idea that it says" for "the wisdom of a person enlightens his face" (line 38). Not checked; reported as said. He reads line 3's ראשין as "rishin", spelled so in the file (gimmel rishin).

Sensitivity: one flag, the remark about Bobby Fischer as a champion who would crush opponents viciously and get sick over losing (named-person; he died in 2008). Left unflagged: the remarks that depression and grief can make a person die (03 w669-823) and that trauma makes a person withdraw (02 w1405-1451), which are observations rather than advice; and the newly frum man who no longer wants to hear non-Jewish music (01 w1769-1885), which disparages no one. A reviewer checked these again for the public edition and left them unflagged: the depression passage states that pain can take away a person's pleasure in life, as the line's klos hanefesh from pain, and gives no advice; the remark that people come to enjoy alcohol or drugs although they are bad for them (04 w2247-2295) is likewise an observation. The Bobby Fischer remark stays flagged with its publishable text.
All four tapes have Sofer's word times, not re-timed ones: the seconds can be off. The word ranges are right.
